metadata.description: Curated waste recycling knowledge base for EcoSwap RAG pipeline
sources: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management & Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016

wasteTypes.description: Corrugated cardboard boxes, packaging materials, cartons, and cardboard sheets. One of the most commonly recycled materials in India, cardboard is a dry waste category under SWM Rules 2016.

steps: Remove all tape, staples, plastic inserts or wax coatings from the cardboard
Flatten all boxes to reduce volume — saves up to 75% storage space
Keep cardboard clean and dry — wet or food-contaminated cardboard must go to composting, not recycling
Segregate from other dry waste as per SWM Rules 2016 three-bin segregation mandate
Hand over segregated dry waste to authorized waste collectors or deposit at designated collection points
At recycling facility: cardboard is pulped with water, cleaned of ink and adhesives, pressed into new sheets
recyclingMethods.tip: Under SWM Rules 2016, waste generators must segregate waste into wet (biodegradable), dry (including cardboard), and domestic hazardous categories before handing to collectors.

steps: Shred non-recyclable or food-contaminated cardboard into small pieces
Mix with green/wet waste in a compost bin
Cardboard adds carbon ('brown material') that balances nitrogen-rich kitchen waste
Compost is ready in 2-4 months
recyclingMethods.tip: Pizza boxes and food-stained cardboard that can't be recycled are excellent for composting. Under SWM Rules 2016, bulk waste generators (>100 kg/day) must compost biodegradable waste on-site.

environmentalFacts.waterSavedPerTon: 7,000 gallons of water saved per ton
environmentalFacts.energySavedPerTon: 4,100 kWh of electricity saved per ton
environmentalFacts.co2ReductionPerTon: 1.5 tons of CO₂ emissions prevented per ton recycled
environmentalFacts.landfillReduction: Recycling 1 ton of cardboard saves 9 cubic yards of landfill space

marketPrice.notes: Price varies by quality, condition, and local market. Clean, dry OCC (Old Corrugated Containers) fetch higher prices. Rates from Indian kabadiwala/scrap dealer markets.

ecoTips: Reuse cardboard boxes for storage or shipping before recycling
One ton of recycled cardboard saves 17 trees and 7,000 gallons of water
Under Swachh Bharat Mission, citizens are encouraged to sell dry waste to kabadiwalas for proper recycling
Keep a separate bin for dry recyclables including cardboard as mandated by SWM Rules 2016

governmentRegulations.applicableRules: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 (MoEFCC Notification S.O. 1357(E))
keyProvisions: Rule 4: Waste generators must segregate waste at source into three categories — biodegradable (wet), non-biodegradable/dry (including cardboard), and domestic hazardous waste
Rule 4(2): No person shall throw, burn, or bury solid waste in open public spaces, streets, drains or water bodies
Rule 4(6): Bulk waste generators (>100 kg/day) must set up in-house waste processing for biodegradable waste
Rule 15: Local authorities must arrange door-to-door collection of segregated waste
Cardboard falls under 'dry waste' category and must be kept separate for recycling
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Every citizen must segregate waste at source into three bins (wet, dry, hazardous) and hand over segregated waste to authorized collectors as per Rule 4 of SWM Rules 2016
governmentRegulations.penalty: Spot fines of ₹200-₹500 for littering; up to ₹5,000-₹1,00,000 for improper waste disposal depending on local municipal bylaws
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: Under draft EPR Rules 2024, packaging manufacturers will be responsible for collecting back packaging waste including cardboard

wasteTypes.description: Glass bottles, jars, containers, and glassware. Glass is 100% recyclable and can be recycled infinitely without loss of quality. It is classified as dry waste under SWM Rules 2016.
wasteTypes.decompositionTime: 1 million+ years in landfill — glass does NOT decompose naturally

steps: Rinse glass containers to remove food residue — a quick water rinse is sufficient
Remove metal lids and caps — recycle these separately as metal waste
Paper labels do NOT need to be removed — they burn off during processing
Sort by color if required by local facility (clear, green, brown/amber)
Do NOT include ceramics, light bulbs, mirrors, window glass, or pyrex — these contaminate glass recycling
Handle broken glass carefully — wrap in newspaper before placing in collection
Deposit at designated glass collection points or hand to authorized collectors
recyclingMethods.tip: Never mix window glass, mirrors, or ceramics with container glass. They have different melting points and will contaminate the recycling batch.

environmentalFacts.co2ReductionPercent: Recycling glass reduces CO₂ emissions by 50% compared to virgin production
environmentalFacts.energySavedPercent: 30% less energy needed compared to making glass from raw materials
environmentalFacts.rawMaterialConservation: Recycled glass (cullet) directly replaces sand, soda ash, and limestone
environmentalFacts.infiniteRecyclability: Glass can be recycled infinite times with zero loss in quality or purity

marketPrice.notes: Glass has lower scrap value compared to other recyclables. Whole bottles fetch more than broken glass. Color-sorted glass commands premium prices.

ecoTips: One ton of recycled glass saves 1,300 pounds of sand, 410 pounds of soda ash, and 380 pounds of limestone
Glass in landfills takes over 1 million years to decompose — always recycle
Reuse glass jars for storage before recycling — reduces demand for new containers
Glass recycling uses 30% less energy than manufacturing from scratch

governmentRegulations.applicableRules: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016; Draft EPR Rules for Packaging 2024
keyProvisions: Glass falls under 'dry waste' category under SWM Rules 2016 and must be segregated at source
Rule 4: Waste generators must segregate into wet, dry, and hazardous categories
Draft EPR Rules 2024: Producers of glass packaging will be required to take back and ensure recycling of glass packaging waste
Local municipal bodies must ensure collection infrastructure for dry waste including glass
Broken glass must be wrapped safely before disposal to prevent injury to waste workers
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Segregate glass as dry waste, rinse containers, wrap broken glass safely, and hand to authorized collectors
governmentRegulations.penalty: Spot fines for littering; fines under local municipal bylaws for improper disposal
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: Under draft EPR framework for packaging (anticipated 2026), glass packaging producers must ensure collection and recycling targets

wasteTypes.description: Aluminum cans, steel containers, tin cans, metal scraps, and ferrous/non-ferrous metal items. Metals are infinitely recyclable without quality degradation and have high scrap value in India.
wasteTypes.decompositionTime: 200-500 years for aluminum; steel can take 50-100 years

steps: Empty and rinse metal containers to remove food residue
Crush cans to save space (optional — saves up to 80% storage volume)
Separate aluminum from steel if possible — use a magnet (steel is magnetic, aluminum is not)
Remove non-metal attachments like plastic labels, rubber seals, or paper wrappings
Do NOT include aerosol cans that are not fully empty — they can explode during processing
Segregate as dry waste and hand to authorized waste collectors or kabadiwalas
At recycling facility: metals are shredded, melted in furnaces at high temperatures, and reformed into new products
recyclingMethods.tip: A used aluminum can returns to the store shelf as a new can in just 60 days — one of the fastest recycling turnarounds of any material.

environmentalFacts.energySavedAluminum: Recycling aluminum saves 95% of the energy needed to make new aluminum from bauxite ore
environmentalFacts.co2ReductionPerTon: Recycling 1 ton of steel prevents 2,500 pounds of iron ore, 1,400 pounds of coal, and 120 pounds of limestone from being mined
environmentalFacts.waterSaved: Recycling metal uses 40% less water than primary production
environmentalFacts.infiniteRecyclability: 75% of all aluminum ever produced is still in use today — metal never degrades through recycling

marketPrice.notes: Prices vary significantly by metal type: Aluminum cans ₹80-120/kg, Steel/Iron ₹25-40/kg, Copper ₹400-600/kg, Brass ₹250-350/kg. Clean, sorted metal fetches higher prices.

ecoTips: Aluminum recycling saves 95% energy — always recycle aluminum cans and foil
Metal has the highest scrap value among common recyclables — sell to local kabadiwalas
Under the Hazardous Waste Rules 2016, metal scrap is regulated for proper handling
One recycled aluminum can saves enough energy to run a TV for 3 hours

governmentRegulations.applicableRules: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management & Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016; Second Amendment Rules, 2024
keyProvisions: Metal scrap (ferrous and non-ferrous) is classified under 'Other Wastes' in Schedule III of the Hazardous Waste Rules 2016

Hazardous Waste Rules 2016 Amendment 2024: Non-ferrous metal producers must incorporate minimum recycled content — 5% from FY 2027-28, increasing to 10% (aluminum), 20% (copper), 25% (zinc) by FY 2030-31
EPR framework introduced for non-ferrous metals — producers must register with CPCB and meet recycling obligations
Steel Scrap Recycling Policy 2019: Framework for establishing metal scrapping centers across India
Vehicle Scrapping Policy 2021 (MoRTH): Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facilities for end-of-life vehicles
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Segregate metal as dry waste, sell to authorized scrap dealers or kabadiwalas, do not mix with hazardous waste
governmentRegulations.penalty: Non-compliance with Hazardous Waste Rules: Environmental compensation under 'Polluter Pays' principle; CPCB may impose separate penalties on industrial non-compliance
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: From FY 2027-28, all non-ferrous metal producers must meet minimum recycled content targets under the 2024 amendment, enforced through EPR certificates issued by CPCB

wasteTypes.description: Newspapers, magazines, office paper, notebooks, paper bags, and similar paper products. Paper is one of the most widely recycled materials and falls under dry waste category.
wasteTypes.decompositionTime: 2-6 weeks for regular paper; coated/laminated paper takes much longer

steps: Remove any plastic windows (from envelopes), plastic coatings, or metal bindings
Keep paper clean and dry — wet, greasy, or food-contaminated paper cannot be recycled
Shred confidential documents — shredded paper is still recyclable
Bundle newspapers and magazines separately if possible
Do NOT include tissues, paper towels, wax paper, or heavily printed thermal receipts in paper recycling
Segregate as dry waste and hand to authorized collectors or sell to kabadiwalas
At recycling facility: paper is pulped with water, de-inked, cleaned of impurities, and pressed into new paper sheets
recyclingMethods.tip: Paper can be recycled 5-7 times before fibers become too short. After that, it can be composted as biodegradable waste.

steps: Shred tissue paper, paper towels, greasy paper, and other non-recyclable paper products
Add to compost bin as 'brown material' (carbon source)
Mix with green/wet waste for balanced composting
recyclingMethods.tip: Tissues, paper towels, and food-stained paper should go to composting, not paper recycling.

environmentalFacts.treesSavedPerTon: 17 trees saved per ton of paper recycled
environmentalFacts.waterSavedPerTon: 7,000 gallons of water saved per ton
environmentalFacts.oilSavedPerTon: 380 gallons of oil saved per ton
environmentalFacts.landfillReduction: 3.3 cubic yards of landfill space saved per ton
environmentalFacts.energySaved: 70% less energy than manufacturing virgin paper

marketPrice.notes: Newspaper ₹7-10/kg, White office paper (sorted) ₹12-16/kg, Mixed paper ₹5-8/kg. Clean, dry paper commands higher prices.

ecoTips: Use both sides of paper before recycling to maximize its lifecycle
One ton of recycled paper saves 17 trees, 7,000 gallons of water, and 380 gallons of oil
Keep paper recycling dry — moisture is the #1 contaminant
Digital alternatives reduce paper consumption — go paperless where possible

governmentRegulations.applicableRules: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016; Hazardous Waste Rules 2016 (waste paper in Schedule III under 'Other Wastes')
keyProvisions: Paper is classified as dry waste under SWM Rules 2016 three-category segregation system
Rule 4: Every waste generator must segregate paper into the dry waste bin
Waste paper is listed in Schedule III of Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules 2016 as 'Other Waste' (B3020) — regulated for transboundary movement
Import of waste paper for recycling is permitted under the rules with proper authorization
Local municipalities must ensure door-to-door collection of segregated dry waste including paper
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Segregate paper as dry waste, keep clean and dry, shred confidential documents, hand to authorized collectors or kabadiwalas
governmentRegulations.penalty: Spot fines for littering; penalties under municipal bylaws for non-segregation
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: Paper packaging will come under EPR framework once the draft EPR Rules for Packaging 2024 are finalized

wasteTypes.description: Plastic bottles, containers, bags, wrappers, and packaging materials. Only 9% of all plastic ever produced has been recycled globally. India has strong plastic waste management rules with single-use plastic bans.

steps: Check the recycling symbol (1-7) on the plastic item — not all plastics are equally recyclable
Rinse containers to remove food residue
Remove caps and labels where possible (caps are often different plastic type)
Crush bottles and containers to save space
Do NOT include styrofoam (expanded polystyrene), plastic-coated paper cups, multi-layer packaging, or thermosetting plastics
Segregate as dry waste and hand to authorized waste collectors
At recycling facility: plastics are sorted by resin type, shredded, washed, melted, and pelletized into raw material
recyclingMethods.tip: PET (Type 1) and HDPE (Type 2) are the most easily recycled plastics. Multi-layer plastic packaging (like chip packets) is extremely difficult to recycle.

steps: Non-recyclable plastic waste can be used as alternative fuel in cement kilns
This is recognized by CPCB as an approved disposal method for plastic waste
Cement kilns operate at temperatures >1400°C, ensuring complete destruction of plastic
recyclingMethods.tip: Under Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016, non-recyclable plastic can be used for road construction or energy recovery in cement kilns.

environmentalFacts.oceanPollution: 8 million tons of plastic enter oceans every year globally
environmentalFacts.recyclingRate: Only 9% of all plastic ever produced has been recycled
environmentalFacts.energySaved: Recycling 1 ton of plastic saves 5,774 kWh of energy
environmentalFacts.oilSaved: Recycling 1 ton of plastic conserves 16.3 barrels of oil
environmentalFacts.decomposition: A single plastic bottle takes 450 years to decompose in landfill

marketPrice.notes: PET bottles ₹12-25/kg, HDPE containers ₹10-20/kg, Mixed plastic ₹5-10/kg. Clean, sorted single-type plastic fetches highest prices.

ecoTips: Refuse single-use plastics whenever possible — they are banned under Indian law
Carry reusable bags, bottles, and containers
Only 9% of plastic ever made has been recycled — reduce consumption is the best strategy
Check the plastic type number (1-7) before recycling — not all plastics can be recycled equally

governmentRegulations.applicableRules: Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 (MoEFCC), amended 2018, 2021, 2022, and 2024
keyProvisions: Single-Use Plastic Ban (effective July 1, 2022): Banned items include plastic plates, cups, straws, cutlery, stirrers, earbuds with plastic sticks, polystyrene for decoration, plastic candy/ice-cream sticks, PVC banners <100 microns, and plastic flags
Carry bag minimum thickness: 120 microns (amended from 50 → 75 → 120 microns)
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR): All producers, importers, and brand owners must register on CPCB portal and meet collection, recycling, and reuse targets
Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2024: Biodegradable plastics require CPCB certification; stricter criteria ensuring no microplastic residue
2024 Amendment: MSMEs exempted from EPR — responsibility shifted to raw material suppliers
Non-recyclable plastic can be used for road construction or co-processing in cement kilns as per CPCB guidelines
From July 2025: Digital traceability (QR codes/barcodes) mandatory on plastic packaging
Local bodies must prevent stocking, distribution, sale, and use of banned single-use plastic items
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Do not use banned single-use plastics; segregate plastic as dry waste; hand to authorized collectors; support EPR by returning packaging to producers
governmentRegulations.penalty: Fine of ₹500-₹25,000 for use/sale of banned single-use plastics under local municipal bylaws; Environmental compensation under 'Polluter Pays' principle for EPR non-compliance by producers
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: Producers must register on CPCB EPR portal (eprplasticwaste.cpcb.gov.in) and meet annual targets for collection, recycling, reuse, and use of recycled content. EPR certificates traded between producers and recyclers.

wasteTypes.description: Mixed or non-recyclable waste that doesn't fit into specific recycling categories. Includes contaminated materials, composite products, and items that cannot be economically recycled.
wasteTypes.decompositionTime: Varies widely — some synthetic materials may never decompose

steps: Identify if any components can be separated for recycling before discarding the entire item
Multi-layer packaging, contaminated recyclables, and composite materials typically go to residual waste
Place in the appropriate bin — usually the general/residual waste bin
Some non-recyclable waste can be sent to waste-to-energy plants
Under SWM Rules 2016, municipalities must ensure scientific disposal of residual waste at sanitary landfills
Never burn waste in the open — it creates toxic fumes and is illegal under SWM Rules
recyclingMethods.tip: Before treating anything as trash, check if components can be separated — a drink carton has paper, plastic, and aluminum that can be recycled if separated.

environmentalFacts.landfillImpact: India generates approximately 62 million tons of solid waste annually; only 43 million tons are collected, and about 12 million tons are treated
environmentalFacts.methaneEmissions: Organic waste in landfills produces methane, a greenhouse gas 28 times more potent than CO₂
environmentalFacts.wasteToEnergy: India has 8 operational waste-to-energy plants processing municipal solid waste

marketPrice.notes: General trash has no market value. However, proper segregation can recover valuable recyclables from mixed waste. RDF produced from non-recyclable waste has some industrial value.

ecoTips: The best way to reduce trash is to reduce consumption and choose products with recyclable packaging
Segregation at source can recover 60-70% of materials from what people typically call 'trash'
Under SWM Rules 2016, open burning of waste is strictly prohibited
Used sanitary products must be wrapped and placed in domestic hazardous waste bin, NOT the dry waste bin

governmentRegulations.applicableRules: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016; SWM Rules 2026 (effective April 1, 2026)
keyProvisions: Rule 4(2) of SWM Rules 2016: Strictly prohibits burning, burying, or throwing solid waste in open public areas
Rule 15: Local authorities must ensure scientific processing and disposal of residual waste
Sanitary waste (diapers, sanitary napkins) must be wrapped securely and placed in domestic hazardous waste bin
SWM Rules 2026 (superseding 2016 rules): Introduces environmental compensation under 'Polluter Pays' principle for non-compliance
Industrial units within 100 km of RDF plants must replace at least 5% of fuel with refuse-derived fuel
Municipalities must establish and operate sanitary landfills for non-recyclable, non-biodegradable waste
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Minimize waste generation; segregate waste properly; do NOT burn or dump waste openly; pay user fees for waste management services
governmentRegulations.penalty: Spot fines ₹200-₹500 for littering; up to ₹1,00,000 for illegal dumping; environmental compensation under Polluter Pays principle in SWM Rules 2026

wasteTypes.description: Discarded electronic and electrical equipment including computers, phones, TVs, appliances, and accessories. E-waste contains valuable recoverable metals (gold, copper, aluminum) but also hazardous substances (lead, mercury, cadmium).
wasteTypes.decompositionTime: Electronics never decompose naturally — hazardous materials leach into soil and groundwater

steps: Do NOT attempt to dismantle electronics yourself — they contain hazardous substances
Back up and wipe all personal data from devices before disposal
Check with the manufacturer or brand for take-back programs (mandatory under E-Waste Rules 2022)
Deposit e-waste at authorized collection centers — check CPCB's registered list
Major brands like Apple, Samsung, Dell, HP have authorized collection points in India
At authorized facility: devices are dismantled, hazardous components separated, and valuable metals (gold, copper, aluminum, iron) recovered
recyclingMethods.tip: Under E-Waste Management Rules 2022, producers are required to take back end-of-life electronics. Check the brand's website for collection points near you.

uses: Recovered gold, copper, aluminum, and iron

environmentalFacts.globalVolume: India generates approximately 3.2 million tons of e-waste annually — 3rd largest generator globally
environmentalFacts.hazardousSubstances: E-waste contains lead, mercury, cadmium, and brominated flame retardants that contaminate soil and water
environmentalFacts.valuableMetals: One ton of circuit boards contains 40-800 times more gold than one ton of gold ore
environmentalFacts.recyclingRate: Less than 20% of global e-waste is formally recycled

marketPrice.notes: Scrap electronics value varies enormously — old phones ₹10-100/piece, computer components ₹20-50/kg, circuit boards ₹200-500/kg (for precious metal content). Only authorized recyclers should process e-waste.

ecoTips: Extend device lifespan through repairs before replacing
Donate working electronics instead of discarding
Never burn or dump electronics — hazardous chemicals contaminate soil and water
Use authorized e-waste collection points — informal recycling exposes workers to toxic materials

keyProvisions: Covers 100+ categories of electrical and electronic equipment including solar PV panels
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR): Producers must achieve recycling targets — 60% of EEE placed on market by FY 2023-24, increasing to 80% by FY 2027-28
All producers, manufacturers, refurbishers, dismantlers, and recyclers must register on CPCB online portal
EPR certificates issued to registered recyclers — tradeable with producers to meet targets
Environmental compensation on 'Polluter Pays' principle for non-compliance
Restriction on hazardous substances (lead, mercury, cadmium) in new electronic equipment
2024 Amendment: Recycling capacity based on installed plant and machinery, up to 20 hours/day; detailed material flow records required
Recognized recycled materials: Gold (Au), Copper (Cu), Aluminum (Al), Iron (Fe)
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Return end-of-life electronics to authorized collection centers or producer take-back programs; do NOT dispose of e-waste with regular household waste
governmentRegulations.penalty: Environmental compensation for non-compliance with E-Waste Rules; CPCB can cancel registration and impose penalties on unauthorized recyclers
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: Check CPCB EPR portal (eprewastecpcb.in) for list of registered e-waste recyclers and authorized collection centers

wasteTypes.description: All types of batteries including dry cell (AA/AAA), lithium-ion, lead-acid, and rechargeable batteries. Batteries contain hazardous chemicals and heavy metals that require specialized recycling.
wasteTypes.decompositionTime: 100+ years — batteries leak toxic chemicals into soil and groundwater as they corrode

steps: Do NOT throw batteries in regular waste bins — they are classified as hazardous waste
Store used batteries in a dry, cool place away from heat and moisture
Cover battery terminals with tape to prevent short circuits during storage
Return batteries to authorized collection points, dealers, or manufacturer take-back programs
Lead-acid batteries (car/UPS/inverter): Return to the dealer or manufacturer
Lithium-ion batteries (phones/laptops): Return to electronics brands or authorized e-waste recyclers
Never attempt to open, crush, incinerate, or dump batteries
recyclingMethods.tip: Under Battery Waste Management Rules 2022, producers and manufacturers must take back used batteries. Check with your battery brand for collection points.

uses: Recovered lithium, cobalt, nickel for new lithium-ion batteries
Recovered zinc, manganese from alkaline batteries

environmentalFacts.leadContamination: One lead-acid battery can contaminate 167,000 liters of water
environmentalFacts.lithiumRecovery: Recycling lithium-ion batteries recovers 95% of materials — critical for EV industry
environmentalFacts.toxicSubstances: Batteries contain lead, cadmium, mercury, lithium, and acid that are highly toxic

marketPrice.notes: Lead-acid batteries ₹40-60/kg (high lead recovery value), Lithium-ion batteries ₹20-40/kg. Never sell to unauthorized dealers.

ecoTips: Use rechargeable batteries to reduce waste
Never dispose batteries with regular household trash
Tape battery terminals before storing for recycling to prevent fire hazards
One lead-acid battery can contaminate 167,000 liters of water if improperly disposed

keyProvisions: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR): Producers must collect and ensure recycling of waste batteries
Prohibition: Waste batteries must NOT be sent for incineration or landfilling
All producers, importers, and recyclers must register on CPCB portal
Collection targets mandated for producers — phased increase over time
Applies to all battery types: lead-acid, lithium-ion, nickel-cadmium, alkaline, zinc-carbon
Dealers and bulk consumers must return used batteries to producers or authorized collection centers
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Return waste batteries to dealers, producers, or authorized collection centers; do not mix with regular household waste; do not burn or bury batteries
governmentRegulations.penalty: Environmental compensation under 'Polluter Pays' principle for non-compliance by producers; penalties for unauthorized recycling operations
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: Producers must set up collection systems and achieve annual collection and recycling targets set by CPCB

wasteTypes.description: Textiles including clothing, fabrics, curtains, towels, bedsheets, and carpets. India's textile industry generates significant waste, and old textiles can be recycled into new products or donated.

steps: Check if clothing/textiles are still wearable — donate to charities or NGOs first
Clean and dry textiles before recycling
Separate by material type if possible (cotton, polyester, blends)
Old cotton clothes can be used as industrial wiping cloths (jhadi/jhaduw)
Panipat (Haryana) is India's largest textile recycling hub — processes discarded garments into blankets (kambal) and shoddy yarn
Damaged textiles can be shredded and used as filling material or insulation
Hand over to kabadiwalas, textile recyclers, or textile collection drives
recyclingMethods.tip: India's Panipat is known as the 'Cast-Off Capital' — it recycles imported second-hand clothing into affordable blankets and fabrics.

environmentalFacts.waterUsage: Producing 1 kg of cotton fabric requires 10,000-20,000 liters of water
environmentalFacts.wasteGenerated: India generates approximately 7.5 million tons of textile waste annually
environmentalFacts.carbonFootprint: The fashion industry is responsible for 10% of global carbon emissions

marketPrice.notes: Cotton waste ₹10-20/kg, Mixed fabrics ₹5-10/kg, Denim waste ₹8-15/kg. Sorted, clean textiles fetch higher rates.

ecoTips: Donate wearable clothes to charities — extend the lifecycle before recycling
Buy quality over quantity — fast fashion is a major environmental problem
Repair clothes instead of discarding — mending extends garment life
India's Panipat recycling industry processes millions of tons of old textiles into useful products

governmentRegulations.applicableRules: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016; Extended Producer Responsibility guidelines (under development)
keyProvisions: Textile waste falls under dry waste category in SWM Rules 2016
MoEFCC is developing EPR framework specifically for textile industry
Swachh Bharat Mission encourages donation and reuse of textiles
National Resource Efficiency Policy promotes circular economy in textiles
BIS standards for recycled fibers in textile products
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Donate wearable textiles; segregate unusable textiles as dry waste; hand to authorized recyclers or kabadiwalas
governmentRegulations.penalty: Under SWM Rules 2016 — spot fines for improper disposal of waste
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: EPR framework for textiles is under development by MoEFCC — expected to mandate producers to take responsibility for end-of-life garments

wasteTypes.description: Biodegradable organic waste including food scraps, vegetable peels, fruit peels, leftover food, garden waste, and yard trimmings. Organic waste constitutes 50-60% of India's municipal solid waste.
wasteTypes.decompositionTime: 2 weeks to 6 months depending on conditions

steps: Segregate organic waste at source — separate from dry and hazardous waste as per SWM Rules 2016
Use a home composting bin — layer green waste (food scraps) with brown waste (dry leaves, cardboard)
Avoid adding meat, dairy, oils, and cooked food with spices in home composting (they attract pests)
Turn the compost pile regularly for aeration
Compost is ready in 45-90 days — it becomes dark, crumbly, and earthy-smelling
Use compost for gardening, potted plants, or community gardens
recyclingMethods.tip: Under SWM Rules 2016, bulk waste generators (>100 kg/day) MUST process biodegradable waste through composting or bio-methanation on-site.

steps: Organic waste is fed into a biogas digester (anaerobic digestion)
Bacteria break down waste in oxygen-free environment producing methane (biogas)
Biogas can be used for cooking fuel or electricity generation
Residual slurry is nutrient-rich fertilizer
recyclingMethods.tip: Community-level biogas plants are promoted under Swachh Bharat Mission and MNRE (Ministry of New and Renewable Energy) schemes.

environmentalFacts.compositionInMSW: Organic waste constitutes 50-60% of India's total municipal solid waste
environmentalFacts.methaneEmissions: Food waste in landfills produces methane — 28 times more potent than CO₂ as a greenhouse gas
environmentalFacts.compostBenefit: Composting returns nutrients to soil and reduces need for chemical fertilizers

marketPrice.notes: Raw organic waste has no market value. Processed compost sells for ₹3-5/kg. Vermicompost fetches ₹5-10/kg. Biogas has energy value.

ecoTips: Compost your kitchen waste — it reduces landfill waste by 50-60%
A simple composting bin can convert kitchen waste into garden-ready compost in 45-90 days
Community biogas plants can power cooking fuel needs from organic waste
Avoid wasting food — India wastes nearly 68.8 million tons of food annually

governmentRegulations.applicableRules: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016; Swachh Bharat Mission Guidelines
keyProvisions: Rule 4: Organic waste must be segregated as 'wet waste' (biodegradable) in the three-bin system
Rule 4(6): Bulk waste generators (hotels, restaurants, institutions generating >100 kg/day or occupying >5,000 sq ft) MUST process biodegradable waste on-site through composting or bio-methanation
Municipalities must promote composting and bio-methanation as primary processing methods
Sale and use of compost products must follow Fertiliser Control Order standards
SWM Rules promote decentralized composting at ward/community level
Swachh Bharat Mission provides financial support for composting infrastructure
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Segregate wet (organic) waste from dry and hazardous waste; compost at home where possible; hand segregated wet waste to authorized collectors
governmentRegulations.penalty: Spot fines for non-segregation; bulk generator penalties for not processing biodegradable waste on-site
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: Composting and bio-methanation are the preferred methods under SWM Rules 2016. Sending biodegradable waste to landfills is discouraged.

wasteTypes.description: Hazardous domestic waste including paints, chemicals, pesticides, cleaning agents, expired medicines, used oil, solvents, and aerosol cans. These require special handling to prevent environmental contamination.
wasteTypes.decompositionTime: Many hazardous chemicals persist indefinitely in the environment

steps: Identify the type of hazardous waste — check product labels for hazard symbols
Store in original containers with labels intact — do NOT mix different chemicals
Keep away from heat, water, and children
Never pour chemicals down drains, toilets, or into regular waste bins
Never burn hazardous waste — it releases toxic fumes
Contact local municipal authority for designated hazardous waste collection days/points
Hand over to authorized Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs)
For expired medicines: return to pharmacies or hospital collection programs
recyclingMethods.tip: Under SWM Rules 2016, domestic hazardous waste must be stored separately in a third bin (red bin) and handed to authorized collectors.

environmentalFacts.groundwaterRisk: Improper disposal of hazardous waste contaminates groundwater — affecting drinking water for millions
environmentalFacts.healthRisk: Exposure to hazardous chemicals causes cancer, neurological damage, and organ failure
environmentalFacts.soilContamination: Chemical waste can render agricultural land infertile for decades

marketPrice.notes: Hazardous waste has no positive market value. Disposal typically incurs a cost. Authorized TSDFs charge processing fees.

commonItems: Nail polish and nail polish remover
ecoTips: Always store hazardous waste separately from regular waste
Never pour chemicals into drains or water bodies
Return expired medicines to pharmacies — many run take-back programs
Switch to eco-friendly cleaning products to reduce hazardous waste generation

governmentRegulations.applicableRules: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management & Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016; SWM Rules 2016 (domestic hazardous waste)
keyProvisions: Domestic hazardous waste (insect repellents, cleaning agents, batteries, CFL bulbs, expired medicines) must be stored in a separate bin (third category under SWM Rules 2016)
Hazardous Waste Rules 2016: All facilities handling hazardous waste must obtain authorization from SPCB (State Pollution Control Board)
Priority hierarchy: Prevention → Minimization → Reuse → Recycling → Recovery → Co-processing → Safe Disposal
Import of hazardous waste for disposal is prohibited; import for recycling requires authorization
TSDFs (Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities) must be authorized and comply with CPCB standards
governmentRegulations.citizenDuty: Segregate domestic hazardous waste in a separate bin; never mix with regular waste; hand to authorized collectors during designated collection events
governmentRegulations.penalty: Criminal liability under sections of Environment Protection Act, 1986; fines ranging from ₹1,00,000 to ₹5,00,000; imprisonment up to 5 years for serious violations
governmentRegulations.eprNotes: Producers of products containing hazardous substances are increasingly being brought under EPR. Battery Waste Management Rules 2022 is an example of this approach.

generalRecyclingGuidelines.description: Cross-cutting recycling guidelines applicable to all waste categories, and fallback information for unknown or unlisted waste types.

threeRs.reduce: Minimize waste generation by avoiding single-use products and buying only what you need
threeRs.reuse: Find new purposes for items before discarding — glass jars for storage, old clothes as cleaning rags
threeRs.recycle: Segregate waste properly and ensure recyclable materials reach authorized recycling channels

segregationBins.description: Under SWM Rules 2016, all waste must be segregated at source into three categories
segregationBins.greenBin: Wet/Biodegradable waste — food scraps, vegetable peels, garden waste
segregationBins.blueBin: Dry waste — paper, plastic, metal, glass, cardboard, textiles
segregationBins.redBin: Domestic hazardous waste — batteries, CFL bulbs, expired medicines, cleaning chemicals, insect repellents, sanitary waste

swachhBharatGuidelines: Every citizen has a duty to segregate waste at source
Do not litter in public places — spot fines applicable
Support your local waste collection system by separating waste daily
Encourage composting of biodegradable waste in your household or community
Use cloth bags instead of plastic bags
Report illegal waste dumping to your local municipal authority

unknownWasteGuidelines.description: Guidelines for handling waste that doesn't match any known category
steps: Check if the item has a material identification label or recycling symbol
Try to identify the primary material — is it paper, plastic, metal, glass, organic, or electronic?
When in doubt, contact your local municipal waste management authority
Many local kabadiwalas (scrap dealers) can identify recyclable materials
If unsure whether an item is hazardous, store separately and consult a waste management expert
Multi-material items (like Tetra Pak cartons) should be checked for local recycling infrastructure
